# Phase 1 — Setup Helper

Run this once to generate the exact `.env` snippet for your Monday boards.

## Step 1 — Create Monday boards (manual, in Monday UI)

**Contacts Board** — one group: "New Active Contacts". Columns:
- Lead Name (text)
- Email (email)
- Email Confidence (dropdown: High)
- Company (text)
- Source (dropdown: Crunchbase, AngelList)
- Date Added (date)
- Status (dropdown: Queued for Outreach, Contacted, Skip)

**Leads Board** — three groups: "New Pipeline", "Qualified Pipe, Reply", "No Response". Columns:
- Lead Name (text)
- Email (email)
- Company (text)
- Status (dropdown: Contacted, Qualified, No Response)
- Send Date (date)
- Subject Line Used (text)
- Email Body Snippet (long text)
- Reply Received Date (date)
- Reply Snippet (long text)
- Follow Up 1 Sent (checkbox)
- Follow Up 2 Sent (checkbox)
- Follow Up 1 Date (date)
- Thread ID (text)

## Step 2 — Get a Monday API token
Monday → avatar → Developers → My Access Tokens → Copy.

## Step 3 — Create n8n credential
n8n → Credentials → New → search "Monday.com" → paste token → save.

## Step 4 — Bootstrap env (minimum two vars)
Add to `docker-compose.yml` under the n8n service, then `docker compose up -d`:

```yaml
environment:
  - MONDAY_CONTACTS_BOARD_ID=123456789
  - MONDAY_LEADS_BOARD_ID=987654321
```

Get the board IDs from each board's URL: `monday.com/boards/<ID>`.

## Step 5 — Attach credential on this workflow
Open the "Monday - Introspect Boards" node below and pick the Monday.com credential you made in Step 3.

## Step 6 — Click Execute Workflow
The final node outputs `dotenv_snippet` — a ready-to-paste block of every remaining env var (group ids + column ids for both boards). Copy it, paste it into docker-compose, restart n8n, and Phase 1 is live.

## After pasting the .env snippet

1. `docker compose up -d` to pick up new env.
2. Verify env vars inside the container: `docker compose exec n8n env | grep MONDAY_`
3. Smoke test each sub-workflow:

### P1.4 Check Duplicate
Execute with test data:
```json
{ "email": "smoke-test@example.com",
  "lead_name": "Smoke Test",
  "company": "Test Co" }
```
Expect `{ is_duplicate: false, matched_on: {...all false} }`.

### P1.1 Add to Contacts Board
```json
{ "lead_name": "Smoke Test",
  "email": "smoke-test@example.com",
  "email_confidence": "High",
  "company": "Test Co",
  "source": "Crunchbase" }
```
Expect `{ item_id: "<number>", success: true }`. Check the Contacts Board — you should see a new item.

### P1.4 again with same data
Expect `{ is_duplicate: true, matched_on: { email_on_contacts: true, ... } }`.

### P1.2 Move to Leads Board
```json
{ "lead_name": "Smoke Test",
  "email": "smoke-test@example.com",
  "send_date": "2026-04-14",
  "subject_line": "Test subject",
  "email_body_snippet": "Test body...",
  "thread_id": "thread-abc-123" }
```
Expect new item on Leads Board, New Pipeline group.

### P1.3 Mark as Qualified
```json
{ "email": "smoke-test@example.com",
  "reply_received_date": "2026-04-14",
  "reply_snippet": "Sounds interesting." }
```
Expect item moved to Qualified Pipe Reply, status = Qualified.

## Clean up test data
Delete the Smoke Test item from Monday before Phase 2 goes live.
